title: Bike Theft in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin lost 22,341 bikes to theft in 2025,** down from 26,758 in 2024 and 34,136 in 2016. The city still accounts for more than a tenth of every reported bike theft in Germany while holding under five per cent of its people.

**The hour in the police file is when the owner last saw the bike,** not when it was taken. Read as a parking clock, 31% of losses were locked up between 18:00 and 22:00 and only 11% between 22:00 and 06:00.
**A third of it is quick.** 32% of thefts happened inside an offence window of three hours or less and 12% inside a single hour, so the errand lock matters more than the overnight one.
**Your district decides which problem you have.** Neukölln loses 36% in the evening band; Marzahn-Hellersdorf loses 25% in the 06:00 to 10:00 commute band against 16% citywide.

**The cellar is not a vault.** 5.1% of Berlin thefts came out of a cellar or bike room, but 11.4% in Spandau and 8.5% in Reinickendorf and Marzahn-Hellersdorf. Lock the frame to something fixed down there too.
**Mitte is roughly four and a half times Spandau.** 1,068 reported thefts per 100,000 residents against 227, for the same bike and the same lock.

**The median bike was declared at €900 and 46% at €1,000 or more.** Check three things in your contents policy before you need them: whether theft away from home is covered, the compensation cap, and any night-time clause.

**Secure station parking is planned and mostly unfunded.** Berlin needs 42,000 more spaces at stations by 2030; Schöneweide is in build, while Ostkreuz, Haselhorst and Landsberger Allee passed their studies and then stalled on money.
